## Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback identifies broad relatedness crowding out specific matches. This motivates testing whether recent, repeated interaction evidence improves next-item ranking; it does not establish latent intent. (2) Existing margins measure separation from sampled training negatives. They cannot establish top-10 accuracy or useful complements. (3) Category metadata and review fields are unavailable despite the generic input examples. Diagnostics must use histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions, and represent missing evidence explicitly.

**Related work.** (1) *Measuring Recency Bias* cautions that stronger recency can reduce accuracy, supporting a learned, ablated contribution rather than mandatory recent-history weighting. (2) Krichene and Rendle show that sampled ranking can reverse model comparisons, so full-catalog diagnostics cannot replace pinned validation selection. (3) ECCR distinguishes compatible complements from co-purchases; titles alone provide incomplete evidence for hard compatibility filtering.

These insights suggest three directions: adaptive history aggregation, controlled history interventions, and evidence-aware compatibility diagnostics.

## Framework

| Direction | Observable evidence | Intervention | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| History aggregation | Ordered training interactions | Learned recent-history residual | Recent activity may be incidental |
| Dependence diagnosis | Natural training prefixes | Equal-size recent/older edits | Sensitivity does not prove usefulness |
| Compatibility diagnosis | Titles/descriptions | Supported/contradicted/unknown labels | Missing prerequisites remain unknown |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Gated recent-interest residual — 4/7/3.** Originality: + combines adaptive aggregation with controlled diagnosis; − closely related to established pooling mixtures. Potential: + directly tests the reported history-weighting weakness; − may duplicate SASRec attention. Difficulty: + adds a small gate and pooling operation; − requires consistent scoring and predictor serialization. Motivated by the recency-bias study.
2. **Paired prefix intervention probe — 3/6/3.** Originality: + connects dependence with held-out training-prefix accuracy; − intervention diagnostics already exist. Potential: + identifies harmful history reliance; − produces no direct ranking improvement. Difficulty: + reuses the scorer; − requires careful matched edits and leakage controls. Motivated by the supplied attribution studies.
3. **Evidence-aware compatibility reranker — 5/5/7.** Originality: + explicit unknown states constrain filtering; − compatibility recommendation is established. Potential: + addresses concrete equipment mismatches; − limited applicability to entertainment. Difficulty: + deterministic evidence is auditable; − reliable parsing across four catalogs is substantial. Motivated by ECCR.

## Selected idea

At 0% progress, select the **gated recent-interest residual**. Combine SASRec’s representation with a normalized mean of the last five nonpadding input embeddings through a learned scalar gate initialized near zero. Train using the baseline objective and negatives, then compare against unchanged SASRec and a fixed-gate ablation.

Retain preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, and the 200-epoch environment default. Select exclusively using pinned macro validation HR@10. Update the predictor writer and compatibility view together; diagnose padding correctness, gate distributions and prefix-intervention accuracy. No improvement is claimed before measurement.

idea.description: Add a small learned recent-history residual to each per-dataset SASRec model. At each valid sequence position, blend the original contextual feature with a normalized mean of up to five preceding input item embeddings, including the current input item. Use the identical blend during training, diagnosis and prediction.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests that incidental or older interactions sometimes overwhelm recent evidence. An adaptive residual provides a low-cost test of this hypothesis while allowing the model to retain its original representation when recent pooling is unhelpful. Histories do not directly reveal intent, ownership, compatibility or satisfaction.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], existing splits, dataset routing, seed settings and trial-local artifacts. Preserve the baseline optimizer, sampling and loss initially to isolate the architecture change. Normalize pooled features using LayerNorm, compute a scalar sigmoid gate from concatenated contextual and pooled features, and initialize the gate bias to -4 with zero gate weights. Mask padding in pooling and loss. Compute all windows causally; no target embeddings may enter their own input windows. Keep padding features zero. Update the generated working/predict.py to recreate and load the gate, pooling normalization and backbone. The compatibility view must expose the actual trained module through view.model and return blended B x L x D features from log2feats; predict_score must support B x L x 2 candidate tensors. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return metrics and metric_definitions, restore the module's original training mode, and report unavailable measurements as null with counts rather than healthy-looking zeros. Use only training-prefix holdouts for auxiliary intervention experiments; exclude their targets from learned auxiliary statistics. Cap auxiliary work because it shares the 43,200 GPU-second budget. Choose checkpoints only through the existing pinned macro validation protocol.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_existing_routes:
    model = existing_SASRec_with_recent_gate()
    for batch in existing_training_loader:
        seq, pos, neg = batch.sequence, batch.positive, batch.negative
        h = model.backbone.log2feats(seq)
        e = model.item_emb(seq)
        r = causal_masked_window_mean(e, seq != 0, width=5)
        r = model.recent_norm(r)
        g = sigmoid(model.gate(concat(h, r)))
        z = ((1 - g) * h + g * r) * (seq != 0)[..., None]
        loss = existing_loss(score(z, pos), score(z, neg), mask=pos != 0)
        optimize(loss)
    save_all_parameters_beneath_trial_directory()
    emit_predictor_with_identical_feature_and_scoring_paths()
select_using_existing_pinned_macro_validation_HR10()

originality.positive: Combines a minimal adaptive history pathway with interventions that test whether its contribution helps next-item ranking.
originality.negative: Gated mixtures and recent-history pooling are established techniques; architectural novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled foundation for learning when short-term evidence helps across distinct recommendation domains.
future_potential.negative: The branch may duplicate SASRec attention, and validation gains would not establish better compatibility or immediate purchase intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a causal pooling operation, normalization and a small scalar gate without additional datasets or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Training, per-position diagnosis and generated inference must share exactly the same causal masking and feature construction.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary reports that excessive recency emphasis can impair recommendation accuracy, motivating adaptive weighting and ablations.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed residual improves the four Amazon datasets.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation — Krichene and Rendle
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-ranking comparisons, motivating strict separation of selection and auxiliary diagnostics.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator or guarantee that a particular loss improves its HR@10.

related_work.title: Explainable and Coherent Complement Recommendation Based on Large Language Models
contributions: Distinguishes relevance and compatibility in complement recommendation.
limitations: Co-purchase and title similarity alone do not establish compatibility, prerequisites or ownership in this task.

related_work.title: Counterfactual Explanations via Genetic Algorithms (2025)
contributions: The supplied summary describes searching for small sequence edits that alter recommendations, motivating history-dependence probes.
limitations: Recommendation changes reveal model sensitivity rather than correctness of inferred user preferences.
